generativity.notes: The deep structure recurs in all five: an fd walk with O_NOFOLLOW, an exclusive temp file plus rename, one writable root, lexical normalisation and E_SHADOW. B and C turn the Structure table into one class per participant, D and E collapse it into policy over primitives, and A sits between with a Root handle and one large Workspace. The details differ where the chapter is silent, and those are the safety-relevant ones. The absolute-path mapping (realpath in A, C, D; lexical in B, E) predicts exactly which ones write through an in-root link. Only A and E guard against overlapping roots, and B, C, D write into a nested read root. Read-link policy differs: C follows in-root links like os.Root, the others refuse all links. The read-protection key differs: identity plus a written exemption in A, B, C; identity and name with no exemption in E; names only in D. Batch nesting has three meanings: A and E share the outer record, B and C give the inner block its own, D refuses nesting. None of the five tracks reads per batch, so NEXT.md's E_IN_USE adds new state everywhere; the implementations with a single read funnel (C _read, E _note_read, B OpenedSet.note_open) absorb it in one place, while A and D record reads in two.

worse_is_better: E. In the probes it has the best containment of the five: no write through an in-root link by absolute path, no write into a nested read root, no shadowing by absolute save. It does this with 851 library lines in two modules, against B's 1309 in ten. It does without a persistent root-handle object and close() lifecycle (A, B, C), separate Locator/Writer/Loader/Location/OpenedSet classes (B, C), require() (A, B, C), C's hand-written link resolver and E_ARG, D's second backend and B's counters. The task needs none of these; the guarantees come from the descriptor walk, the exclusive temp plus rename, lexical absolute matching and one overlap check. E's own extras (the nlink refusal, a name set beside the identity set) add restriction rather than machinery. What it lacks (a written-exemption set, roots named in refusal text) is a few lines. A is the runner-up: as safe except for absolute saves through in-root links, and better for the agent (own output can be re-saved, refusals name the roots), at the cost of a larger Workspace.
chapter_lessons: Name the overlapping-roots force. Note 7's own example is a read root mounted inside the workspace, but nothing says writes beneath it must be refused. B, C and D let save('mounted/x') write into the read root (probe), B even tests the configuration (impl-B/tests/test_save.py:240-245). Only A (impl-A/jailfs/_workspace.py:419-429) and E (impl-E/jailfs/workspace.py:121-128) guard it. Say: refuse overlapping roots at start-up.

Resolve links in trusted configuration, never in agent paths. 'Make a symlinked read root resolve to its target' (note 7) led A, C and D to realpath the agent's absolute path (impl-A/jailfs/_workspace.py:294, impl-C/jailfs/locator.py:130, impl-D/jailfs/workspace.py:233), which lets an absolute save write through an in-root link. B and E canonicalise roots once and match agent paths lexically against both spellings (impl-B/jailfs/root.py:115-120, impl-E/jailfs/workspace.py:47-52), and their walk stays honest.

Say what the opened set protects. Once writes never follow links and always rename, a save cannot change an input's inode: B's test (impl-B/tests/test_boundaries.py:18-26) and E's docstring (impl-E/jailfs/fsops.py:11-14) state it, and D's name-only ledger leaves data intact in the probe. What the set protects is the agent's view (do not clobber what you read). Without this, implementations over-reach: E refuses every nlink>1 file (impl-E/jailfs/workspace.py:334-340), and D and E refuse to re-save their own output.

Present participants as responsibilities, not classes, and mark the sketch's goja-specific parts. B and C built one module per Structure-table row and B carries a dozen dead members (impl-B/jailfs/loader.py:22-23, locator.py:118-123). A, B and C transcribed require() and C transcribed E_ARG (impl-C/jailfs/errors.py:26) for a task with no module system. D and E reach equal or better containment with two layers.

Note 6 should say the shadow check applies to the resulting relative name however it is spelled. C exempts absolute saves (impl-C/jailfs/workspace.py:166-167), and its own test loads a shadowed helper (impl-C/tests/test_loader.py:22-29): this is the library-shadowing trap the note says goja-cv avoided.

Define the run scope. Duplicate saves (note 10) are per call in the chapter and per batch in the task, and nesting came out three ways (A/E share, B/C inner scope, D refuses). No implementation scoped reads to a run, so a run-scoped rule like E_IN_USE is new state in all five. The chapter should say the session holds a stack of runs and that per-run read and write sets belong to it.

Note 11 needs a technique, and the Applicability warning needs to be louder. Only B automated 'fail without the fix' (impl-B/tools/regression_check.py), and its class-level granularity hid a vacuous identity test that stays green under the identity mutation (impl-B/tests/test_save.py:174-181). D shipped the string-check fallback the Applicability section warns against (impl-D/jailfs/fsio.py:361-543).
